---
title: "Principal component analysis"
---

Principal component analysis (PCA) finds directions along which centered rows vary. For the PHOIBLE matrix, a row is an inventory record and a column is a segment listing. PCA thus summarizes covariance among database-segment columns. It does not use phonological labels, family names, or macroareas to fit the directions.

## Beginning with variation around column means

Let

$$
\mathbf Z
=
\mathbf X
-
\mathbf 1_n\widehat{\boldsymbol\mu}^{\mathsf T}
$$

be the training-centered matrix. For a unit direction $\mathbf v$, the row scores are

$$
\mathbf t=\mathbf Z\mathbf v.
$$

Their sample variance is

$$
\operatorname{Var}[\mathbf t]
=
\frac{1}{n-1}\mathbf t^{\mathsf T}\mathbf t
=
\mathbf v^{\mathsf T}
\left(\frac{\mathbf Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Z}{n-1}\right)
\mathbf v.
$$

Define the sample covariance matrix

$$
\mathbf S
=
\frac{\mathbf Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Z}{n-1}.
$$

The first principal-component direction solves

$$
\mathbf v_1
=
\arg\max_{\mathbf v^{\mathsf T}\mathbf v=1}
\mathbf v^{\mathsf T}\mathbf S\mathbf v.
$$

Later directions maximize the same criterion while remaining orthogonal to the preceding directions.

## Connecting PCA to the SVD

If

$$
\mathbf Z=\mathbf U\mathbf D\mathbf V^{\mathsf T},
$$

then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf S
&=\frac{1}{n-1}\mathbf Z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf Z\\
&=\frac{1}{n-1}
\mathbf V\mathbf D\mathbf U^{\mathsf T}
\mathbf U\mathbf D\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}\\
&=\mathbf V
\frac{\mathbf D^2}{n-1}
\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus the PCA directions are the right singular vectors, and the covariance eigenvalues are

$$
\lambda_k=\frac{d_k^2}{n-1}.
$$

The component scores satisfy

$$
\mathbf T
=
\mathbf Z\mathbf V
=
\mathbf U\mathbf D.
$$

This is an identity between two computations, not a resemblance inferred from a plot.

## Verifying the identity on PHOIBLE

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

phoible <- readRDS("data/phoible/phoible-pilot.rds")
inventories <- phoible$inventories[
  order(phoible$inventories$glottocode,
        as.integer(phoible$inventories$inventory_id)),
]
groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(inventories)), inventories$glottocode)
RNGkind(sample.kind = "Rejection")
set.seed(20260827L)
chosen <- vapply(groups, function(x) x[[sample.int(length(x), 1L)]], integer(1))
selected <- inventories[unname(chosen), ]

area <- selected$macroarea
area[is.na(area) | area == ""] <- "Unclassified"
selected$split <- NA_character_
set.seed(20261018L)
for (name in sort(unique(area))) {
  index <- sample(which(area == name))
  n_holdout <- floor(0.15 * length(index))
  selected$split[index[seq_len(n_holdout)]] <- "validation"
  selected$split[index[n_holdout + seq_len(n_holdout)]] <- "test"
  selected$split[index[is.na(selected$split[index])]] <- "training"
}
training_rows <- which(selected$split == "training")

memberships <- merge(
  phoible$memberships,
  selected[c("inventory_id", "glottocode")],
  by = c("inventory_id", "glottocode")
)
frequency <- table(
  memberships$segment_id[memberships$glottocode %in%
    selected$glottocode[training_rows]]
)
column_ids <- sort(names(frequency)[frequency >= 20L])
X <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(selected),
  ncol = length(column_ids),
  dimnames = list(selected$glottocode, column_ids)
)
retained <- memberships[memberships$segment_id %in% column_ids, ]
X[cbind(
  match(retained$glottocode, rownames(X)),
  match(retained$segment_id, colnames(X))
)] <- 1

training_mean <- colMeans(X[training_rows, , drop = FALSE])
Z <- sweep(X[training_rows, , drop = FALSE], 2, training_mean, "-")
decomposition <- svd(Z)
covariance_fit <- eigen(crossprod(Z) / (nrow(Z) - 1), symmetric = TRUE)
svd_eigenvalues <- decomposition$d^2 / (nrow(Z) - 1)
scores_from_V <- Z %*% decomposition$v
scores_from_UD <- sweep(decomposition$u, 2, decomposition$d, "*")

c(
  maximum_eigenvalue_difference =
    max(abs(covariance_fit$values - svd_eigenvalues)),
  maximum_score_difference = max(abs(scores_from_V - scores_from_UD))
)
```

The largest eigenvalue difference is `r format(max(abs(covariance_fit$values - svd_eigenvalues)), scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`. The largest difference between the two score calculations is `r format(max(abs(scores_from_V - scores_from_UD)), scientific = TRUE, digits = 3)`. These discrepancies reflect floating-point arithmetic.

## Plotting scores, then adding metadata

Macroarea did not enter the matrix, centering, SVD, or covariance calculation. We add it only after fitting to ask whether the unsupervised coordinates display broad descriptive differences.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.5

score_data <- data.frame(
  PC1 = scores_from_V[, 1],
  PC2 = scores_from_V[, 2],
  macroarea = selected$macroarea[training_rows]
)
score_data$macroarea[
  is.na(score_data$macroarea) | score_data$macroarea == ""
] <- "Unclassified"

ggplot(score_data, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey25", alpha = 0.42, size = 0.65) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  facet_wrap(~macroarea) +
  labs(x = "PC1 score", y = "PC2 score") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank())
```

The score clouds overlap substantially. Any apparent macroarea pattern may combine inventory size, source practices, genealogy, geography, and typological organization. The figure cannot distinguish those explanations because macroarea is neither a modeled cause nor the unit of the split.

## Interpreting the variance criterion narrowly

PCA maximizes variance in the supplied representation. Here that representation contains centered binary listings for training-retained segments. A direction with high variance is not necessarily the best direction for reconstruction of hidden cells, classification, or a linguistic theory. Those targets require an external criterion.

PCA also does not discover a group contrast merely because groups can be colored after fitting. If a labeled contrast is the target, the evaluation must withhold appropriate units and assess it directly.

## Checking the variance direction

1. Why must the matrix be centered before this covariance interpretation?
2. What quantity does $\mathbf v^{\mathsf T}\mathbf S\mathbf v$ measure?
3. Why are $\mathbf V$ and $\mathbf D^2/(n-1)$ the covariance eigenvectors and eigenvalues?
4. Which metadata enter the fit on this page?
5. Why can the macroarea facets not isolate a causal explanation?
